mainTopic: How רב and שמואל explain the משנה's comparison of שור and מבעה, and how each reading fits the משנה's wording
overview: This amud continues explaining the משנה's line 'לא הרי השור כראי המבעה' and the dispute between רב, who reads מבעה as אדם, and שמואל, who reads it as שן. First, in a reading where שור means קרן, the גמרא tries to show why קרן and שן must both be listed. A קל וחומר based on intent seems to make קרן unnecessary. רב אשי rejects the slave comparison offered to defend it, then shows that each category has its own stricter feature: קרן has intent, and שן has pleasure. That reading falls because it leaves out רגל. So רבא explains instead that שור means רגל and מבעה means שן. He says קרן is not named because the opening list covers only damagers that are מועד from the start. The גמרא then asks why שמואל rejects רב's reading, and both sides explain why אדם is named again later in the משנה. Finally, the גמרא defends רב against the משנה's wording: 'not like' points to כופר and ארבעה דברים, 'their normal way to damage' means a מועד ox and a sleeping person, and 'their guarding is upon you' is answered with רבי אבהו's reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Eating has no intent to harm, unlike Goring
steps.stepSummary: The reading of the משנה continues: שן is different from קרן because שן does not mean to cause damage, while קרן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the nature of שן, which does not intend to damage, is not like the nature of קרן, which does intend to damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how the משנה's comparison between categories shows that שן and קרן are different. It points to one difference: intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that eats someone's produce is just eating; it is not trying to hurt anyone. An animal that gores is trying to cause harm. This difference is offered as the reason one category cannot be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Nature or defining feature (literally 'appearance')
Tooth: damage an animal causes by eating
Horn: damage an animal causes by goring
Its intention is to cause damage

phrases.english: And the characteristic of Tooth (Eating) is not
where it does not intend to cause damage,
like the characteristic of Horn (Goring),
where it does intend to cause damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא רְאִי הַשֵּׁן – שֶׁאֵין כַּוּוֹנָתוֹ לְהַזִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of the משנה that began before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שן lacks intent to damage, while קרן has it, so the two are distinguished.

steps.title: Goring could be learned from Eating by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if שן is liable without intent, then קרן, which has intent, should obviously be liable. So why would the תורה need to list קרן separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a קל וחומר? If שן, which does not intend to damage, is liable, then קרן, which does intend to damage, should certainly be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the difference just given. The difference about intent actually seems to prove that קרן can be learned from שן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference given in step 1 makes קרן look worse than שן. If the lighter case (שן, with no intent) is already liable, the more serious case (קרן, with intent) should be liable all the more. That would make a separate category for קרן unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a more serious case
'If even...' (opens a קל וחומר)
Liable to pay
Not all the more so?

phrases.english: But isn't it an a fortiori (kal vachomer) argument?
If Tooth,
which does not intend to damage, is liable,
then Horn, which does intend to damage,
is it not all the more so liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the difference given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the intent difference keeps קרן and שן separate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The intent difference makes קרן more serious, so קרן should follow from שן by a קל וחומר and would not need its own category.

steps.title: Goring was needed because of the slave comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תורה had to state קרן. Otherwise we might have exempted it, just as an owner is exempt when his slave deliberately causes damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought it is like a slave or maidservant: even though they mean to cause damage, the owner is still exempt. So too here, it would be no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the need for a separate category of קרן. It shows a reason we might have wrongly exempted the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A master does not pay when his עבד ואמה damages on purpose. Based on that, we might think that deliberate damage by something you own is exempt. So the תורה had to say clearly that the owner of a goring animal is liable, and the קל וחומר alone would not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
You might have thought to say
Just as it is in the case of
A slave and a maidservant
They (the owners) are exempt

phrases.english: It was necessary,
as it would have entered your mind to say:
it is just like a slave and a maidservant.
A slave and a maidservant: is it not so that
even though they intend to cause damage,
even so, their owners are exempt?
So too here, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reason we might have thought otherwise, which makes the extra category necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Deliberate damage by something one owns is exempt, as with a slave
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה lists קרן to teach that the owner of a goring animal is liable

steps.title: רב אשי: the slave exemption has its own special reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the slave comparison. A master is exempt for his slave's damage only because otherwise an angry slave could ruin his master, and that reason has nothing to do with animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Do slaves really not have a big reason of their own? If the master were liable, the master might anger the slave, and the slave would go burn another person's grain stack. He would make his master owe a hundred מנה every day!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי knocks down the answer from step 3. The slave case cannot teach us anything about animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave's exemption is a special protection for the master against revenge, not a general rule that deliberate damage is exempt. An animal cannot plot revenge, so no one would have compared קרן to a slave. The answer of step 3 falls, and the קל וחומר problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (a sharp rhetorical question)
A strong, special reason
He will anger him
A stack of harvested grain
A coin worth one hundred זוז

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a master is not liable for his slave's damages: the rule protects him from revenge. It is not a statement about deliberate damage in general.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Is that to say that a slave and maidservant
don't have a strong reason of their own?
Perhaps his master will anger him,
and he will go and set fire to another person's grain stack,
and it turns out this slave makes his master liable for
a hundred maneh every day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַטּוּ עֶבֶד וְאָמָה לָאו טַעְמָא רַבָּה אִית בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole slave comparison used to justify listing קרן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The slave exemption rests on a special reason (fear of revenge) that does not apply to animals

steps.title: New reading: each category has its own stricter feature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה. קרן is stricter because it intends harm, and שן is stricter because it enjoys the damage. Since each has a feature the other lacks, neither can be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה argues like this: קרן, which intends to damage, is not like שן, which does not. And שן, which gets pleasure from its damage, is not like קרן, which gets no pleasure from its damage.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the slave answer failed, the גמרא changes how the משנה's comparison is read. This new reading blocks learning in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first reading, both differences made קרן look worse, which invited a קל וחומר. Now each side gets its own stricter feature: קרן has intent, and שן has pleasure. You cannot learn שן from קרן, because שן has no intent. You cannot learn קרן from שן, because קרן has no pleasure. So both must be listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach)
It argues (refutes) this way
Pleasure from its damage

steps.whatToRemember: In this reading, קרן is stricter because of intent, and שן is stricter because of pleasure, so neither can be learned from the other. But this whole reading (שור = קרן) is about to be challenged in steps 6–8 because it leaves out רגל.
steps.confusionAlert: The two clauses look almost the same as in step 1, but the features have been swapped. Before, each clause named a category's weaker feature. Now each clause names a category's stronger feature, and that is what blocks the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rather, it refutes like this:
The characteristic of Horn is not
where it intends to cause damage,
like the characteristic of Tooth,
where it does not intend to cause damage;
and the characteristic of Tooth is not
where there is pleasure in its damage,
like the characteristic of Horn,
where there is no pleasure in its damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuing his statement from step 4, רב אשי replaces the failed reading of step 1 with a reformulation that blocks the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the משנה so that each category has a separate stricter feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קרן could be learned from שן by a קל וחומר based on intent
steps.terutzMaskana: Each category has its own stricter feature, so neither can be learned from the other, and both are needed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Within the reading that שור = קרן, intent makes קרן stricter and pleasure makes שן stricter. This reading is later rejected (steps 6–8).

steps.title: Where is Trampling in this reading?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה lists only קרן and שן, then רגל seems to be missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about רגל? Did the משנה leave it out?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from the previous steps. If the משנה names only קרן and שן, it seems to skip רגל, which is also a main category of damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is supposed to list the four main categories of damage. Under the reading that שור means קרן and מבעה means שן, nothing in the list stands for רגל. Leaving out a main category would be a serious gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Foot: damage an animal does while walking, like trampling
He left it out (omitted it)
What (about)?

phrases.english: And what about Foot (Trampling)?
Did he leave it out?!
phrases.notes: 'He' is the author of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading set up in step 5 by pointing out a category it leaves out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה's שור means קרן and מבעה means שן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A list of the main damages cannot leave out רגל, yet this reading has no place for it.

steps.title: The closing line includes Trampling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's closing phrase 'כשהזיק חב המזיק' is what brings in רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'when it damages, the one who caused damage is liable' are there to include רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רגל is not really missing. It is included by the general line at the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing words 'כשהזיק חב המזיק' are general and could cover more than the named cases. The answer reads them as quietly adding רגל to the list. So the משנה includes רגל without naming it.

keyTerms.meaning: When it damages, the one who caused damage is liable (the closing line of the משנה)
To include, to bring in

phrases.english: "When it damages, the one who caused damage is liable"
is there to include Foot (Trampling).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by pointing to a general phrase in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a general phrase in the text that covers the missing case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רגל seemed to be left out of the משנה entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: רגל is included through the general closing phrase.

steps.title: Then it should have said so openly
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה wanted to include רגל, it should have named it outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה just teach it openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. רגל is a main category, so it makes no sense to include it only through a vague closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hinting at a lesser detail through a general phrase is reasonable, but רגל is one of the four main categories. Hiding a main category in an extra phrase is not believable. This challenge knocks down the whole reading, and that is why רבא now starts again with 'אלא'.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him teach it
Openly, explicitly

phrases.english: But let him teach it explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 7, which ends the reading that שור means קרן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רגל is included only through 'כשהזיק חב המזיק'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A main category would be named openly, not slipped in through a general phrase.

steps.title: רבא: שור means רגל, מבעה means שן
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the משנה differently: שור stands for רגל and מבעה stands for שן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The משנה taught 'שור' to mean its foot, and 'מבעה' to mean its tooth.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier reading failed, רבא offers a new one. In his reading the two words in the משנה refer to רגל and שן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that the earlier reading is dropped. In the old reading שור meant קרן. Now רבא says שור means רגל, so רגל is named openly in the משנה, which answers the problem of step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach)
A word in the משנה, read here as שן (Eating)
Tooth: damage an animal does by eating

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The tanna taught "Ox" to refer to its foot,
and "Maveh" to refer to its tooth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: תְּנָא שׁוֹר – לְרַגְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed reading with a new one in which רגל is named openly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads what the words of the משנה refer to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שור meant קרן, so רגל was missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: שור means רגל and מבעה means שן.

steps.title: How Foot and Tooth differ
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the contrast in the משנה: רגל happens often, and שן involves enjoyment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: רגל, whose damage happens often, is not like שן, whose damage does not happen often. And שן, where the animal enjoys the damage, is not like רגל, where it gets no enjoyment from the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now fits his reading into the משנה's wording 'לא ראי זה כראי זה'. He names a feature that only רגל has and a feature that only שן has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רגל is more common, because an animal walks all the time. שן is the one the animal enjoys. Since each has its own feature, you could not learn one from the other, so the משנה needed to name both. This is the same kind of reasoning as step 5, now applied to רגל and שן.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it is saying
The nature of this one is not like the nature of that one
Common, happens often
Enjoyment, benefit

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's reading, שור is רגל and מבעה is שן. רגל is common, and שן brings the animal enjoyment. Because each has its own feature, neither can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
The nature of Foot, whose damage is common, is not
like the nature of Tooth, whose damage is not common;

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא רְאִי הַשֵּׁן – שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֲנָאָה לְהֶזֵּיקוֹ,
phrases.english: and the nature of Tooth, where there is enjoyment in its damage, is not
like the nature of Foot, where there is no enjoyment in its damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: לֹא רְאִי הָרֶגֶל – שֶׁהֶזֵּיקָהּ מָצוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's reading by explaining the משנה's contrast between the two categories.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the contrast in the משנה so it fits the new reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear how 'לא ראי זה כראי זה' fits רגל and שן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רגל is common, and שן involves enjoyment, so each needed to be listed.

steps.title: Now where is Goring?
steps.stepSummary: In רבא's reading, קרן now seems to be missing from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about קרן? Did the משנה leave it out?!
steps.whatsHappening: The same question now hits רבא's reading. If שור is רגל and מבעה is שן, the משנה seems to skip קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 6. Fixing the gap for רגל opened a new gap for קרן. The גמרא is checking whether רבא's reading has the same weakness as the old one.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn: damage an animal does on purpose, like goring

phrases.english: And what about Horn (Goring)? Did he leave it out?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's new reading in the same way step 6 challenged the old one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that שור means רגל and מבעה means שן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A list of the main damages cannot leave out קרן, yet this reading has no place for it.

steps.title: The closing line includes Goring
steps.stepSummary: In רבא's reading, the closing phrase 'כשהזיק חב המזיק' is what brings in קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'when it damages, the one who caused damage is liable' are there to include קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as in step 7, now for קרן. The general closing line of the משנה includes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same answer that was used for רגל in step 7. Back in step 8 that answer was rejected with 'let him teach it explicitly'. So a learner should watch whether the same push-back will come up here.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer has the same form as step 7, which was rejected in step 8. Don't assume the matter is settled yet; watch what the גמרא does next.

phrases.english: "When it damages, the one who caused damage is liable"
is there to include Horn (Goring).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by reusing the method of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a general phrase in the text that covers the missing case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קרן seemed to be left out of רבא's reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: קרן is included through the general closing phrase.

steps.title: Why not mention Goring outright?
steps.stepSummary: If the closing phrase of the משנה is meant to include קרן, the משנה should have named קרן plainly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the משנה teach it openly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 12. If the משנה really wants to include קרן, why does it only hint at it instead of naming it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12, קרן was found only inside the closing phrase 'כשהזיק חב המזיק.' The גמרא asks why such a major category would be tucked into a general phrase. It is the same kind of challenge as Step 8, which asked the same thing about רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach it (let the משנה say it)
Explicitly, openly, by name

phrases.english: But let him teach it explicitly!
phrases.notes: 'It' means קרן, which Step 12 found hidden in the closing phrase of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קרן is included only through the phrase 'כשהזיק חב המזיק'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A main category of damage should be listed by name, not hinted at in a general phrase.

steps.title: The opening only lists damagers that are forewarned from the start
steps.stepSummary: The opening of the משנה lists only damagers that are מועד from the start. קרן starts out תם and becomes מועד only later, so it is not named there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about damagers that are מועד from the beginning. It is not talking about damagers that start out תם and only later become מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opening list has one theme: damagers that are fully liable from the very first time. קרן does not fit that theme, so it is only hinted at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שן, רגל, בור and אש are מועד from the start, so the owner pays full damages the first time. קרן starts out תם, with only half damages, and becomes מועד after goring three times. So leaving קרן's name out of the list is on purpose, not a gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Forewarned from the start; full payment from the first time
Innocuous; at first the owner pays only half damages
It is talking about

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean קרן is not a main category of damage. It is a full אב, but its legal pattern is different: it starts as תם and becomes מועד only later.

phrases.english: It speaks of those forewarned from the outset;
about those innocuous and ultimately forewarned,
it does not speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the theme of the list so the omission makes sense
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should name every main category.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening list covers only damagers that are מועד from the start, so קרן is only hinted at.

steps.title: Why doesn't שמואל agree with רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל does not explain מבעה as אדם, the way רב does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל, what is his reason for not saying like רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches sides. It has been working through שמואל's reading, that מבעה is שן, and now it asks why שמואל did not simply read מבעה as אדם, like רב. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads מבעה as אדם, and שמואל reads it as שן. The גמרא wants to know what is wrong with רב's reading in שמואל's eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Like רב

phrases.english: And Shmuel, what is the reason
he did not say like Rav?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why doesn't שמואל explain מבעה as a person, the way רב does?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from working out שמואל's reading (מבעה is שן) to asking why שמואל rejects רב's reading (מבעה is אדם)
steps.sheelahInformationSought: שמואל's reason for not explaining מבעה as אדם

steps.title: Man is listed separately later in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל points out that a later משנה names אדם on its own, so אדם was probably not already in the opening list as מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: if you think מבעה means אדם, look at the later part of the משנה. It says: an ox that is מועד, an ox that damages in the injured person's property, and a person!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the later משנה lists אדם separately. That makes it unlikely that the opening already listed אדם under the name מבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אדם had already been taught at the start, the later mention would be a repeat. The fact that the later משנה names אדם suggests it was not mentioned earlier. So מבעה must mean something else, which for שמואל is שן.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)
The later part of the משנה
An ox that is forewarned
The property of the injured person

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָדָם,
phrases.english: He would say to you: if it enters your mind that it is Man,
isn't it taught in the latter clause:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה later in the perek, on דף ט״ו ע״ב.

phrases.english: a forewarned ox,
and an ox that damages in the domain of the injured party,
and the man!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The later משנה lists אדם separately, which suggests it was not already taught in the opening as מבעה.

steps.title: Then why not list Man at the start?
steps.stepSummary: If אדם is a main category, why didn't the opening משנה list it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it teach אדם in the first part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל. If אדם is a real category of damage, it should have been in the opening list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reading leaves אדם out of the opening list. The גמרא asks why the משנה would skip it there and name it only later.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: But let him teach it in the first clause!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's reading from Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading, which leaves אדם out of the opening list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A main category like אדם should appear in the opening list.

steps.title: The opening covers only damage done by one's property
steps.stepSummary: The opening משנה is about damage caused by a person's property, not damage he does with his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about damage caused by one's property. It is not talking about damage done by one's own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opening list has a set theme: things a person owns that cause damage. A person hurting with his own body is a different kind of case, so it is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ox, pit and fire are all property that the owner is responsible for. אדם is the person himself doing the damage. That is why, on שמואל's view, אדם waits for the later משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Damage caused by one's property
Damage done by one's own body

phrases.english: It speaks of damages by property;
of damages by one's body it does not speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the theme of the list so the omission makes sense
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every main category should be in the opening list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening list covers only damage by property, so אדם is left for later.

steps.title: The same problem for רב
steps.stepSummary: רב also has to explain why the later משנה names אדם again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רב too: isn't אדם taught in the later part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns שמואל's proof back on רב. If מבעה already means אדם, why is אדם named again later?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the argument from Step 16, now aimed directly at רב. On רב's reading, the later mention of אדם looks like a needless repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: And Rav too,
isn't Man taught in the latter clause!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נָמֵי, הָא קָתָנֵי אָדָם בְּסֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the evidence from Step 16 to challenge רב
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading that מבעה means אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אדם was already taught at the start, naming it again later would be a pointless repeat.

steps.title: The later mention of Man counts it among the forewarned
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the later משנה mentions אדם for a new reason: to count it in the list of damagers that are מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would tell you: that later mention comes to count אדם together with the damagers that are מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the later mention is not a repeat. It has its own job: to put אדם on the list of מועדין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה is a list of מועדין. אדם is named there to teach that a person is always treated as מועד for damage he does. So the mention adds new information, and רב's reading still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To count it, to include it in a list
Together with

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of מבעה survive. For שמואל, as רבא explains him, the opening משנה skips קרן's name because it lists only damagers that are מועד from the start. It also skips אדם because it deals only with damage by property, so אדם appears only later. For רב, the later mention of אדם is there to count it among the מועדין.

phrases.english: Rav would say to you:
That one is to count it
together with the forewarned that it comes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: הָהוּא לְמֶחְשְׁבֵיהּ בַּהֲדֵי מוּעָדִין הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the repeated mention its own new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Naming אדם again later would be a pointless repeat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later mention teaches that אדם belongs on the list of מועדין.

steps.title: What does 'not like' mean according to רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב explains the משנה's line that שור is not like מבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'is not like' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה's comparison 'the ox is not like the מבעה' means, if we follow רב. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, שור already covers every kind of ox damage, and מבעה is a person. So the old way of contrasting them no longer fits. The גמרא needs a new difference between an ox and a person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is not like.' The משנה's wording for showing that two categories differ
One of the four main damagers. For רב, it means a person (אדם)

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of 'is not like'?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the opening משנה: 'the ox is not like the מבעה.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending why אדם is named again in the later משנה, the גמרא now checks the opening משנה's own wording against רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What difference between שור and מבעה (אדם) the משנה has in mind, according to רב.

steps.title: Ox pays ransom; a person pays four extra payments
steps.stepSummary: Each category has a payment the other lacks: שור pays כופר, and אדם pays ארבעה דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: an ox, whose owner pays the ransom, is not like a person, who does not pay the ransom. And a person, who is liable for four extra payments, is not like an ox, which does not have those four payments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the משנה is pointing to a payment that only one of the two damagers has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ox's owner pays כופר when the ox kills someone, but a person who kills does not pay כופר. A person who injures pays ארבעה דברים, but an ox's owner pays only for the damage. Since each has its own payment, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom paid by the owner of an ox that killed a person
Nature or defining feature
Four payments a person owes for injuring someone, beyond the damage itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב's reading of the משנה working. The contrast between שור and מבעה is about how each one pays, not about how the damage happens.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
The nature of the ox is not,
where [the owner] pays the ransom,
phrases.notes: This is the ransom for an ox that kills a person (שמות 21:30).

phrases.english: like the nature of a person,
who does not pay the ransom;
and the nature of a person is not,
who is liable for four things,
phrases.notes: These are pain, medical bills, lost work and embarrassment, which a person pays on top of the damage.

phrases.english: like the nature of the ox,
which does not have the four things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is in what each one pays: שור pays כופר and אדם does not, while אדם pays ארבעה דברים and שור does not.

steps.title: Is it normal for an ox to cause damage?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says all the damagers normally cause damage, but goring, which רב includes in שור, is not normal for an ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: The common feature of them is that they normally cause damage. But is it normal for an ox to cause damage?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the opening משנה and challenges רב with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, שור includes goring (קרן). A regular ox does not usually gore. So how can the משנה say that שור normally causes damage?

keyTerms.meaning: The common feature shared by several cases
It is their normal way to cause damage
'But is it really so?' It opens a surprised challenge

phrases.english: The common feature among them
is that their normal way is to cause damage.
But is it an ox's normal way to cause damage?!
phrases.notes: He means goring. רב counts goring as part of שור, and goring is not what an ox usually does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'not like' clause to the משנה's closing 'common feature' clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that שור in the משנה includes goring
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says every listed damager normally causes damage. Goring is not normal for an ox, so שור should not include goring.

steps.title: The משנה means a מועד ox
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about an ox that is already מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a מועד ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's ox is a מועד, an ox that has already been warned about goring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם ox does not normally gore. A מועד ox has a record of goring. The answer limits the משנה's claim to the מועד ox.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox known as a gorer after goring repeatedly
An ox with no record of goring

phrases.english: With a forewarned [ox].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific kind of ox
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean every ox, and most oxen do not gore.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a מועד ox, which has a record of goring.

steps.title: Is goring normal even for a מועד?
steps.stepSummary: Even a מועד ox is not born a gorer, so how is goring its normal way?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it a מועד ox's normal way to cause damage?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling an ox מועד only means it has gored a few times. That does not obviously make goring its nature. So 'normal way' still seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn. The category of goring damage
Its normal way

phrases.english: And is a forewarned [ox]'s normal way to cause damage?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה means a מועד ox
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מועד ox gored a few times, but that does not make goring its natural way.

steps.title: Once warned, goring has become its way
steps.stepSummary: Once an ox has become מועד, goring counts as its normal behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has been warned, goring is its way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a pattern of goring turns goring into the ox's normal behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Normal way' does not have to mean how the ox was born. It can mean a habit the ox has built. A מועד ox has shown that goring is now its way.

keyTerms.meaning: It was warned, meaning it became מועד
It is its way or its habit
Since; once

steps.whatToRemember: For רב, the 'normal damage' of שור fits goring only when the ox is a מועד, because its repeated goring has become its habit.

phrases.english: Since it has been forewarned,
it is its way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines 'normal way' as a habit the ox has built
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Normal way' seemed to mean the animal's natural behavior.
steps.terutzMaskana: A repeated pattern of goring makes goring the ox's way.

steps.title: Is it normal for a person to cause damage?
steps.stepSummary: If מבעה is אדם, how can the משנה say it normally causes damage?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it a person's normal way to cause damage?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the same 'normally damaging' line against רב's view that מבעה is a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not usually go around damaging things. So calling אדם a damager by nature seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A person. For רב, this is the meaning of מבעה
To cause damage

phrases.english: Is it a person's normal way to cause damage?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same challenge from step 23 to the second category, אדם.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that מבעה is אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says each damager normally causes damage, but a person does not normally cause damage.

steps.title: The משנה means a sleeping person
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about damage a person causes while asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a person who is asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's case of אדם is a sleeping person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An awake person controls himself. A sleeping person moves without control. That is where damage can be his normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is asleep

phrases.english: With a sleeping [person].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to mean every person, and people do not normally damage.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a sleeping person.

steps.title: Is a sleeper's damage normal?
steps.stepSummary: Even a sleeping person does not normally cause damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it a sleeping person's normal way to cause damage?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer about a sleeping person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sleep is not a time when people usually break things. So the claim of 'normal way' still seems shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: His normal way is to cause damage

phrases.english: Is it a sleeping [person]'s normal way to cause damage?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה means a sleeping person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sleeping people do not usually cause damage either.

steps.title: A sleeper curls and stretches, so damage is normal
steps.stepSummary: A sleeping person curls up and stretches out, so damaging what is near him is his normal way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he curls up and stretches out, it is his way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a sleeper's movements make damage a normal result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While asleep, a person keeps bending and stretching his limbs. Anything lying next to him can easily get hit. So damage is a normal part of how a sleeper behaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Curls up; bends his limbs
Stretches out

steps.whatToRemember: For רב, both שור and אדם fit the משנה's 'they normally damage.' שור fits as a מועד ox, and אדם fits as a sleeping person.

phrases.english: Since he curls up and stretches out,
it is his way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows why damage is a normal result in this situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sleeping person seemed not to damage things normally.
steps.terutzMaskana: A sleeper's curling and stretching makes damage to nearby things normal for him.

steps.title: A person is not guarded by someone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that מבעה means אדם. The משנה says 'their guarding is upon you,' but a person is responsible for guarding himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'And their guarding is your responsibility'?! A person is responsible for guarding his own body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge against reading מבעה as אדם, based on the משנה's wording 'ושמירתן עליך.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists features shared by all the main categories of damage. One of them is that 'you' must guard them. That fits an ox or a pit, which an owner watches over. It does not fit a person, because no one is in charge of guarding another adult; each person must watch himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding, keeping watch so that no damage happens
'And their guarding is upon you': one of the shared features listed in the משנה
His body, meaning his own self
Upon him, meaning it is his own responsibility

phrases.english: "And their guarding is upon you"?!
A person: the guarding of his body is upon himself!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמִירָתָן עָלֶיךָ אָדָם שְׁמִירַת גּוּפוֹ עָלָיו הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא answered the 'normal damage' problem (Step 30), it attacks the reading of מבעה as אדם from another phrase in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that מבעה in the משנה means אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says all the categories are guarded by 'you,' the owner. A person has no owner guarding him. He guards himself, so אדם does not fit the משנה's wording.

steps.title: The same question would hit קרנא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: קרנא's ברייתא clearly lists אדם as one of the four categories, yet it uses the same wording. So the question cannot prove that מבעה is not אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about the ברייתא that קרנא taught: 'There are four main categories of damage, and a person is one of them'? There too we can ask: a person is responsible for guarding his own body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with 'ולטעמיך': your question would also hit a source that clearly counts אדם as a category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרנא's ברייתא says outright that אדם is one of the four categories, and it shares the same 'guarding' wording. So the wording cannot mean that אדם is not included. The question is a problem for everyone, so it cannot be used to reject reading מבעה as אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning': turns the questioner's logic back on him
קרנא, a sage who taught a ברייתא about the categories of damage
The main categories of damage

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question yet. It only shows that the question is not a reason to reject reading מבעה as אדם. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
that which קרנא taught:
Four main categories of damage,
and a person is one of them;
a person: the guarding of his body is upon himself!
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes קרנא's ברייתא also says 'their guarding is upon you,' so the same question applies there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 31 by showing that its question would equally hit קרנא's ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the 'guarding' wording as a reason to say that מבעה cannot be אדם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question proves too much. קרנא's ברייתא clearly includes אדם and still has the same wording.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's reading: a person guards himself
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי אבהו, the wording is read so that for אדם, the guarding is his own responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is as רבי אבהו said to the reciter of ברייתות: Teach it this way: 'A person: the guarding of his body is upon himself;'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer. It brings רבי אבהו's instruction on how to recite the ברייתא, and applies it to the משנה as well. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו told the reciter to read the line so that, for אדם, the guarding falls on the person himself, not on someone else. So 'guarding' is still a shared feature, but for אדם it works differently: he must watch himself. This removes the problem, and מבעה can still mean אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: introduces the real answer
Here: a reciter in the study hall who memorized and repeated ברייתות

steps.whatToRemember: For אדם, the duty to guard is real, but it falls on the person himself. So the wording of the משנה can still include אדם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps reading מבעה as אדם alive. It also shows that one shared feature can apply in a different way to different categories.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לְתַנָּא:
phrases.english: Rather, as רבי אבהו said to the reciter:
Teach: A person: the guarding of his body is upon himself;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ לְתַנָּא תְּנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing that the question applies to קרנא's ברייתא too (Step 32), the גמרא gives the real solution that works for both sources.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: the text is recited so that it fits אדם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their guarding is upon you' seemed to mean someone else guards every category, so אדם would not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אדם, the guarding is on the person himself. So אדם fits the shared feature, and מבעה can mean אדם.
